statement: For every even integer n>=2, for the sets M_n defined verbatim in source.md and precisely in problem.md, there exists c_n with M_n=[-c_n,1+c_n] and (sqrt(2)-1)/2<=c_n<1-1/sqrt(2). At t=-c_n, Q_(n,t) has exactly one double zero r in (-1,0), all other zeros are simple and smaller than r, partial_z^2 Q_(n,t)(r)>0, and partial_t Q_(n,t)(r)<0; the other endpoint has the reflected configuration. The proof establishes the following operator theorem: if -3/10<=t<0, h has even degree d>=2, positive leading coefficient, and d simple zeros in (-1,0), S=h'(0)/h(0), delta=(1+2t)/(1+t)^2, and 0<lambda<=1/(S+delta), then T_t^2[(z-lambda)h] has d+2 simple zeros in (-1,0) and one simple positive zero, where T_t p=z(1+z)p'+(z+t)p. Equality in the lambda bound is included. Consequently every odd Q_(m,t), m>=1, has m-1 simple zeros in (-1,0) and one simple positive zero for -3/10<=t<0. The original successive-nesting assertion c_n<=c_(n+2) is not claimed and remains unresolved.
contribution: A uniform Cauchy--Schwarz sign estimate for a coefficient-constrained two-step Eulerian operator closes the exterior odd-degree induction and proves the interval-shape part of Vishnyakova Conjecture 5.8 in all even degrees, with endpoint collision classification. This is an all-degree partial theorem, not another finite-degree calibration. The limited current primary-source screen found no equivalent in the inspected material; novelty and correctness require a fresh referee. No sharpness of -3/10 and no resolution of successive nesting are claimed.
